narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 27.0%. Although that is not a high percentage, it was above the cutoff used for this application, so the loan was denied. The most influential factor was the short requested term: you asked for 6 months, compared with an average of about 19 months among approved applicants, and this worked in your favor. The second most influential factor was your credit-history rating of “critical/other credits”; in your case it also counted in your favor, even though that rating appears among about 33% of approved applicants. The third and most important factor pushing against you was your checking-account status of below 0 DM. That position is uncommon among approved applicants—only about 12.6% fall into that category—so it was the main top-ranked signal toward bad credit risk. Taken together, the checking-account signal and other details in your profile outweighed the helpful signals from the short term and credit history. Next, ask the lender to confirm the account information used and provide recent statements if anything is inaccurate. Reducing any overdraft or negative balance, building savings, and asking whether a guarantor or co-applicant would be considered are practical steps before reapplying or requesting reconsideration.
